name: fairy queen

attributes.attribute: helped Cormac MacCarthy win a lawsuit
told MacCarthy to kiss the stone at dawn
talked his way out of trouble through glibness
placed in an out-of-reach part of the castle wall
attracts tourists who hang upside down to kiss it

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The fairy queen is a folkloric figure tied to a local ruler. After Cormac MacCarthy asked her for help in winning a lawsuit, he kissed the stone at dawn as Clidna instructed. The kiss gave the man fluent speech, and he won free of the legal fix. He set the stone in a far corner of the castle wall so others could not gain the same gift. It stays there today. Tourists hang upside down to kiss it and seek Clidna's favor.

okr.objective: The fairy queen grants a gift of fluent speech through a stone.
